full_judgment:
20. Now let us see what is the law regarding the burden of proof. Section 101 of the Evidence Act lays down the provision of the burden of proof which runs thus- 

 When a person is found to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof lies on that person." 

 21. The burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who desires it. It is reasonable and just that the suitor, who relies upon the existence of a fact, should be called upon to prove his own case. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish his case and he cannot, on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his right and clearness of his own proof. 

 27. On the other hand, the contesting defendants examined 2 DWs, DW 1 Abdul Sabur Howlader is defendant No. 12 and DW 2 Chan Fakir is a contiguous land holder. DW 1 deposed in support of the contention of the contesting defendants and DW 2 deposed corroborating the evidence of DW 1. Furthermore, the contesting defendant Nos. 19 and 22 have submitted the certified copy of the order sheet dated 23-12-1986 in Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 1986 marked Exhibit E, the certified copy of the order sheet and solenama in review Miscellaneous Case No.2 of 1994 marked Exhibits B and B 1; and the certified copy of RS khatian No. 172 Exhibit C and SA khatian No. 225 and 183 Exhibits D and D1. All these documents clearly prove the title of Rupsha Fakir by virtue of auction purchase. The kabuliyats dated 1st Shrobon, 1326 BS in favour ofImanuddin by Rupsha Fakir Exhibit A and dakhila Exhibit G (1 to 9) and the kabala dated 23-7-1937 executed by Rupsha Fakir in favour of Abdur Sabur Exhibit A 1 also evidently speaks of the title of the contesting defendants in the suit land. In view of the above facts and evidence on record, we are of the view that the plaintiffs have totally failed to prove their case and their predecessor's title in the suit land has been extinguished by the auction sale of the suit land for arrears of rent and thus the contesting defendants have proved the basis of RS and SA record in respect of the suit land by filing the valid papers of auction sale, Dakhalnama and boynama and the contesting defendants have proved their title by filing and proving the title deeds like kabuliyats, Dhakhilas, kabala and other relevant papers. It is the established principle of law that the party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish his case and he cannot, on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and the clearness of his own proof. Here in this case the plaintiffs in order to succeed must have to prove their title and possession in the suit land and they can stand on the weakness of the defendants. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, it is evident that the plaintiffs have totally failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land. Moreover, the case of the contesting defendants is so strong that they cannot even stand on the weakness of their adversary's case. Further- more, it appears from record that defendant Nos. 19, 20 and 22 have made a compromise with the plaintiffs which has no basis and, as such, this compromise appears to be illegal, collusive and fraudulent for which this sort of compromise does not create any title in the suit land.
